transcript.text: Welcome, everyone. As you know, I've been asked to restore a worn 1920s community cookbook. The cookbook has a detached cover and several loose pages. Before I decide whether to accept the commission and set final terms, I'd like to hear from each of you regarding any terms, offers, or material constraints you'd like to stated for the record, as is our usual workshop practice. Please go ahead.

transcript.text: I'd like to put a barter proposal on the record. Inez, if you'll reattach the cover, resew the loose sections, and make a simple cloth spine, I'll provide twelve archival linen sheets plus $40. I'd bring the book Tuesday at 18:00 and collect it Saturday at 16:00.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I'd like to put my own offer on the record. I've offered Inez $320 cash for a separate two-week restoration of a family recipe ledger, and that offer remains open.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I'd like to put a material constraint on the record. I previously inspected this cookbook for a local archivist, who confirmed that its brittle acidic pages require wheat-starch paste and Japanese tissue for the loose-page repairs. Ordinary PVA glue should not be used.
